#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# export.sh — repository context dump for LLM consumption, at docs/llm/dump.txt.
#
#   bash export.sh
#
# Dumps only git-tracked files, excluding itself; its source appears once, in the
# self-documentation section. Three kinds of path are held out, and the kinds are distinct
# because other gates care about the difference:
#
#   GENERATED_DIRECTORIES  tool output, never authored. scripts/check_tree.sh skips these too.
#   ARCHIVED_DIRECTORIES   authored history, withheld to keep the dump small. Still tracked, still
#                          hygiene-checked. A session cannot see these, so every archived document
#                          must be linked by path from a document the dump does contain.
#   ELIDED_FILES           metadata and SHA-256 only, body replaced by one line.
#
# Emits per-file relative path, size and SHA-256 — deliberately no absolute path, mtime,
# permissions, owner or last commit. Builds into a temporary file and renames atomically, so a
# reader can never observe a partially written dump.
#

set -euo pipefail
IFS=$'\n\t'

export LC_ALL=C

SCRIPT_PATH="$(readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"
SCRIPT_DIRECTORY="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
SCRIPT_NAME="$(basename "$SCRIPT_PATH")"

if ! git -C "$SCRIPT_DIRECTORY" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree &>/dev/null; then
    exit 0
fi
if ! git -C "$SCRIPT_DIRECTORY" status --porcelain &>/dev/null; then
    exit 0
fi
REPOSITORY_ROOT="$(git -C "$SCRIPT_DIRECTORY" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || exit 0

GENERATED_DIRECTORIES=("docs/llm")

ARCHIVED_DIRECTORIES=("docs/progress")

ELIDED_FILES=("LICENSE")

EXCLUDED_FILES=("$SCRIPT_NAME")
EXCLUDED_FILES_DISPLAY="$(printf '%s, ' "${EXCLUDED_FILES[@]}")"
EXCLUDED_FILES_DISPLAY="${EXCLUDED_FILES_DISPLAY%, }"

EXCLUDED_PATHS_DISPLAY="$(printf '%s/, ' "${GENERATED_DIRECTORIES[@]}" "${ARCHIVED_DIRECTORIES[@]}")"
EXCLUDED_PATHS_DISPLAY="${EXCLUDED_PATHS_DISPLAY%, }"

ELIDED_FILES_DISPLAY="$(printf '%s, ' "${ELIDED_FILES[@]}")"
ELIDED_FILES_DISPLAY="${ELIDED_FILES_DISPLAY%, }"

OUTPUT_DIRECTORY="${REPOSITORY_ROOT}/${GENERATED_DIRECTORIES[0]}"
OUTPUT_FILE="${OUTPUT_DIRECTORY}/dump.txt"

iso_timestamp() {
    date --iso-8601=seconds 2>/dev/null || date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z'
}

TIMESTAMP="$(iso_timestamp)"
GIT_BRANCH="$(git -C "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_COMMIT="$(git -C "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_COMMIT_SHORT="$(git -C "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_COMMIT_MESSAGE="$(git -C "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" log -1 --pretty=format:'%s' 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_COMMIT_DATE="$(git -C "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" log -1 --pretty=format:'%ci' 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
GIT_REMOTE="$(git -C "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || echo 'none')"
GIT_STATUS_SUMMARY="$(git -C "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" status --short 2>/dev/null | head -20 || echo '')"

mapfile -t RAW_TRACKED_FILES < <(
    git -C "$REPOSITORY_ROOT" ls-files --cached -z 2>/dev/null \
    | tr '\0' '\n' \
    | sort -u
)

is_elided_file() {
    local candidate="$1" entry
    for entry in "${ELIDED_FILES[@]}"; do
        [[ "$candidate" == "$entry" ]] && return 0
    done
    return 1
}

INCLUDED_FILES=()
for candidate_file in "${RAW_TRACKED_FILES[@]}"; do
    [[ -z "$candidate_file" ]] && continue
    candidate_in_excluded_tree=0
    for excluded_prefix in "${GENERATED_DIRECTORIES[@]}" "${ARCHIVED_DIRECTORIES[@]}"; do
        [[ "$candidate_file" == "${excluded_prefix}/"* ]] && { candidate_in_excluded_tree=1; break; }
    done
    (( candidate_in_excluded_tree )) && continue
    candidate_excluded=0
    for excluded_entry in "${EXCLUDED_FILES[@]}"; do
        if [[ "$excluded_entry" == */* ]]; then
            [[ "$candidate_file" == "$excluded_entry" ]] && { candidate_excluded=1; break; }
        else
            [[ "$candidate_file" == "$excluded_entry" || "$candidate_file" == */"$excluded_entry" ]] && { candidate_excluded=1; break; }
        fi
    done
    (( candidate_excluded )) && continue
    INCLUDED_FILES+=("$candidate_file")
done

FILE_COUNT="${#INCLUDED_FILES[@]}"
if (( FILE_COUNT == 1 )); then
    FILE_COUNT_NOUN="file"
else
    FILE_COUNT_NOUN="files"
fi

human_size() {
    local bytes="$1"
    if (( bytes < 1024 )); then
        printf '%d B' "$bytes"
        return 0
    fi
    awk -v bytes="$bytes" 'BEGIN {
        unit_count = split("KiB MiB GiB TiB PiB", units, " ")
        value = bytes
        unit_index = 0
        while (value >= 1024 && unit_index < unit_count) {
            value = value / 1024
            unit_index = unit_index + 1
        }
        printf "%.1f %s", value, units[unit_index]
    }'
}

file_sha256() {
    local path="$1"
    if command -v sha256sum &>/dev/null; then
        sha256sum "$path" | awk '{print $1}'
    elif command -v shasum &>/dev/null; then
        shasum -a 256 "$path" | awk '{print $1}'
    else
        echo 'unavailable'
    fi
}

is_binary_file() {
    local path="$1"
    local mime_type
    if command -v file &>/dev/null; then
        mime_type="$(file --brief --mime-type "$path" 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
        case "$mime_type" in
            text/*|image/svg+xml|application/json|application/xml|application/x-yaml|application/yaml|application/javascript|application/x-shellscript|application/x-empty|inode/x-empty)
                return 1
                ;;
            image/*|audio/*|video/*|font/*|application/octet-stream|application/zip|application/gzip|application/x-tar|application/pdf)
                return 0
                ;;
        esac
    fi
    local nul_byte_count
    nul_byte_count="$(head -c 8192 "$path" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '\0' | wc -c)"
    (( nul_byte_count > 0 ))
}

build_file_tree() {
    if (( FILE_COUNT == 0 )); then
        printf '.\n(no files included)\n'
        return 0
    fi
    if command -v tree &>/dev/null; then
        printf '%s\n' "${INCLUDED_FILES[@]}" \
        | tree --fromfile -a --noreport --charset=UTF-8 2>/dev/null \
        || render_tree_fallback
    else
        render_tree_fallback
    fi
}

render_tree_fallback() {
    printf '.\n'
    render_tree_level "" ""
}

render_tree_level() {
    local parent_path="$1"
    local prefix="$2"

    local -a child_names=()
    local previous_child=""
    local entry remainder child_name
    for entry in "${INCLUDED_FILES[@]}"; do
        if [[ -n "$parent_path" ]]; then
            [[ "$entry" == "${parent_path}/"* ]] || continue
            remainder="${entry#"${parent_path}"/}"
        else
            remainder="$entry"
        fi
        child_name="${remainder%%/*}"
        if [[ "$child_name" != "$previous_child" ]]; then
            child_names+=("$child_name")
            previous_child="$child_name"
        fi
    done

    local child_count="${#child_names[@]}"
    local child_index child_path connector descendant_prefix child_is_directory
    for (( child_index = 0; child_index < child_count; child_index++ )); do
        child_name="${child_names[$child_index]}"
        if (( child_index == child_count - 1 )); then
            connector='└── '
            descendant_prefix="${prefix}    "
        else
            connector='├── '
            descendant_prefix="${prefix}│   "
        fi
        if [[ -n "$parent_path" ]]; then
            child_path="${parent_path}/${child_name}"
        else
            child_path="$child_name"
        fi
        child_is_directory=0
        for entry in "${INCLUDED_FILES[@]}"; do
            if [[ "$entry" == "${child_path}/"* ]]; then
                child_is_directory=1
                break
            fi
        done
        if (( child_is_directory )); then
            printf '%s%s%s/\n' "$prefix" "$connector" "$child_name"
            render_tree_level "$child_path" "$descendant_prefix"
        else
            printf '%s%s%s\n' "$prefix" "$connector" "$child_name"
        fi
    done
}

print_file_metadata() {
    local relative_path="$1"
    local file_size="$2"
    local sha256_value="$3"

    printf '\n--- METADATA ---\n'
    printf '  %-22s %s\n' "Relative path:" "$relative_path"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n' "Size:"          "$(human_size "$file_size") (${file_size} bytes)"
    printf '  %-22s %s\n' "SHA-256:"       "$sha256_value"
    printf '\n--- CONTENT ---\n'
}

print_file_content() {
    local absolute_path="$1"
    local file_size="$2"
    local sha256_value="$3"
    local relative_path="${4:-}"

    if [[ -n "$relative_path" ]] && is_elided_file "$relative_path"; then
        printf '[Elided — unmodified boilerplate, %s, SHA-256 above. The bytes are in the tree.]\n' \
            "$(human_size "$file_size")"
        return 0
    fi

    if is_binary_file "$absolute_path"; then
        printf '[Binary file — content omitted. Size: %s, SHA-256: %s]\n' \
            "$(human_size "$file_size")" "$sha256_value"
        return 0
    fi

    cat "$absolute_path"
    if [[ -s "$absolute_path" ]] && (( $(tail -c 1 "$absolute_path" | wc -l) == 0 )); then
        printf '\n'
    fi
}

generate_dump() {
    cat <<BANNER
################################################################################
#                                                                              #
#   REPOSITORY CONTEXT DUMP                                                    #
#   Generated for LLM consumption — do not edit manually                       #
#                                                                              #
################################################################################

DUMP METADATA
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  Generated at   : ${TIMESTAMP}
  Generator      : ${SCRIPT_NAME}

REPOSITORY METADATA
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  Repository root: ${REPOSITORY_ROOT}
  Branch         : ${GIT_BRANCH}
  Commit (full)  : ${GIT_COMMIT}
  Commit (short) : ${GIT_COMMIT_SHORT}
  Commit date    : ${GIT_COMMIT_DATE}
  Commit message : ${GIT_COMMIT_MESSAGE}
  Remote origin  : ${GIT_REMOTE}
  Files included : ${FILE_COUNT}
  Withheld paths : ${EXCLUDED_PATHS_DISPLAY}
  Excluded files : ${EXCLUDED_FILES_DISPLAY}
  Elided files   : ${ELIDED_FILES_DISPLAY} (metadata and SHA-256 only)

NOT EVERYTHING TRACKED IS BELOW
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  The withheld paths above hold tracked, authored files that are NOT in this
  dump. docs/progress/ is the earlier half of the build log; it is real, it is
  in git, and it is linked by path from docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md. Do not
  reconstruct a withheld file from this dump and do not deliver a withheld
  file's sibling as though it were the whole document.

GIT WORKING TREE STATUS (first 20 lines)
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BANNER

    if [[ -n "$GIT_STATUS_SUMMARY" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$GIT_STATUS_SUMMARY"
    else
        echo "  (clean — no uncommitted changes)"
    fi

    cat <<SELF_HEADER

################################################################################
# FILE: ${SCRIPT_NAME}  [THIS SCRIPT — included for full context]
################################################################################
SELF_HEADER

    local script_relative_path script_size script_sha256
    script_relative_path="$(realpath --relative-to="$REPOSITORY_ROOT" "$SCRIPT_PATH" 2>/dev/null || echo "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
    script_size="$(wc -c < "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
    script_sha256="$(file_sha256 "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
    print_file_metadata "$script_relative_path" "$script_size" "$script_sha256"
    print_file_content  "$SCRIPT_PATH" "$script_size" "$script_sha256" "$script_relative_path"

    cat <<TREE_HEADER

################################################################################
# FILE TREE  (${FILE_COUNT} included ${FILE_COUNT_NOUN})
################################################################################
TREE_HEADER

    build_file_tree
    echo ""

    local total_bytes=0
    local relative_path absolute_path file_size sha256_value
    for relative_path in "${INCLUDED_FILES[@]}"; do
        absolute_path="${REPOSITORY_ROOT}/${relative_path}"

        [[ -f "$absolute_path" ]] || continue

        file_size="$(wc -c < "$absolute_path" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
        total_bytes=$(( total_bytes + file_size ))
        sha256_value="$(file_sha256 "$absolute_path")"

        printf '\n'
        printf '################################################################################\n'
        printf '# FILE: %s\n' "$relative_path"
        printf '################################################################################\n'
        print_file_metadata "$relative_path" "$file_size" "$sha256_value"
        print_file_content  "$absolute_path" "$file_size" "$sha256_value" "$relative_path"
    done

    cat <<FOOTER

################################################################################
# DUMP SUMMARY
################################################################################
  Files dumped   : ${FILE_COUNT}
  Total size     : $(human_size "$total_bytes") (${total_bytes} bytes)
  Output file    : ${OUTPUT_FILE}
  Completed at   : $(iso_timestamp)
################################################################################
# END OF DUMP
################################################################################
FOOTER
}

mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIRECTORY"

TEMPORARY_FILE="$(mktemp "${OUTPUT_DIRECTORY}/.dump.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$TEMPORARY_FILE"' EXIT

generate_dump > "$TEMPORARY_FILE"

chmod 644 "$TEMPORARY_FILE"
mv -f "$TEMPORARY_FILE" "$OUTPUT_FILE"
trap - EXIT

cat "$OUTPUT_FILE"

# What the image builder is allowed to see (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §14.1).
#
# Containerfile's build stage runs `COPY . .`, so this file decides what "." means. Read by both
# engines: Docker/BuildKit reads `.dockerignore` from the context root, and Podman reads
# `.containerignore` or `.dockerignore` from the same place (ADR-0004 makes rootless Podman
# canonical, and CI builds with Docker — one file has to satisfy both, and this is it).
#
# WHY AN ALLOW-LIST RATHER THAN A DENY-LIST. A deny-list answers "what is wrong today". The thing
# that put this file here (F-45) is that `.gitignore` is a deny-list, that it is already correct,
# and that it protects nothing here — a build context is not a commit, and every path it names was
# being copied into the builder anyway. A deny-list would have to be extended for tomorrow's
# untracked secret by somebody who remembered to. This list has to be extended for tomorrow's
# *source directory*, by a build that fails immediately when it is not.
#
# The guard in Containerfile asserts this file took effect, because an ignore-file is an
# instruction to a tool and instructions can be renamed, superseded by a `.containerignore`, or
# overridden with `--ignorefile`. The two lists are deliberately stated twice: if they drift, the
# build stops.

# ---- everything ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
*

# ---- ...except the publish graph -------------------------------------------------------------------
# `dotnet publish src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.csproj` needs the three
# source projects, the two Directory.*.props files that central package management resolves through,
# global.json for SDK selection, and .editorconfig because EnforceCodeStyleInBuild reads it — so the
# image build and the CI build apply the same analyzer set.
!.editorconfig
!Directory.Build.props
!Directory.Packages.props
!global.json
!src

# ---- ...and never local build output, even from inside src -----------------------------------------
# A workstation that has run `dotnet build` leaves these behind. They are git-ignored and were
# therefore invisible to every gate in this repository, while being copied into the builder on every
# `podman-compose --profile production up -d --build`. Last matching line wins, so these come after
# the re-inclusion above.
src/**/bin
src/**/obj

--- METADATA ---
  Relative path:         .env.example

# Copy to `.env` and adjust. `.env` is git-ignored; never commit a populated one.
# Configuration is environment-only (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §13). Every value here has a safe dev
# default in the app; the ones marked "PRODUCTION: change" MUST be overridden before going live.

# --- Identity & origin ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
RESTAURANT_NAME=My Restaurant
# The canonical origin for QR/link URLs and the fallback for the WebAuthn RP ID. Dev uses Caddy on
# 8443; production is your Cloudflare named-tunnel hostname (a stable domain so passkeys persist).
# PRODUCTION: change (must be an https URL). The RP ID is derived per request from the host the
# browser is on (ADR-0005), so a quick tunnel's per-run *.trycloudflare.com host works too — this
# value is the fallback when a request carries no trusted Origin header.
RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://localhost:8443
# Wildcard origins (besides RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN and loopback) allowed to act as the WebAuthn
# relying party (ADR-0005, §3.3). Comma/space/newline separated; each is scheme://host with an
# optional single leading "*." label, https, no path or port. The default trusts Cloudflare quick
# tunnels so `scripts/quick_tunnel.sh` demos work with passkeys out of the box; clear it (set to a
# single space) to lock passkeys to RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN only.
RESTAURANT_TRUSTED_ORIGIN_PATTERNS=https://*.trycloudflare.com
# The restaurant's IANA zone. EVERY instant the application renders — order times, the footer clock,
# an administrator's audit column — is shown in this zone, for every viewer, wherever they are (§8.1).
# A guest abroad checking last week's bill sees the times the meal actually happened at.
RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE=America/New_York
# How those times are written: "12-hour" (3:04 PM) or "24-hour" (15:04). Display only; it decides
# nothing about what is stored. Before this existed the choice came from whatever locale the container
# image happened to carry, which is to say from nobody (F-36).
RESTAURANT_CLOCK_FORMAT=12-hour
RESTAURANT_CURRENCY_CODE=USD
# Where this instance's source code is published (§11.9). Linked from /source, which the footer of
# every page links to. If you have MODIFIED this program and run it as a network service, AGPL-3.0-only
# §13 requires you to offer your users the corresponding source — point this at your fork and you have
# done so:
#
#     RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL=https://git.example.com/you/myrestaurant
#
# Absolute http or https; http is accepted here (unlike RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN) so a self-hosted
# forge on a LAN is not refused.
#
# ASSIGNED EMPTY, and that is F-50's ruling applied to this file rather than an omission. Empty means
# "the program's own default", which is RestaurantOptions.DefaultSourceUrl and the ONE place the
# fallback is written down — the reason compose.yaml passes this variable through with an empty default
# too. This file previously spelled the upstream URL here, which is the same defect one layer over: a
# fork whose first edit is that constant would have had it silently overridden by the `.env` they were
# told to copy, and served their users a §13 offer pointing at somebody else's repository.
RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL=

# --- Database ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Consumed by the postgres container. PRODUCTION: change POSTGRES_PASSWORD.
POSTGRES_USER=myrestaurant
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=myrestaurant
POSTGRES_DB=myrestaurant
# The app's own connection string. In compose this is derived from the POSTGRES_* values above and
# points at the `postgres` service; only set this if you are pointing at an external database.
# RESTAURANT_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING=Host=postgres;Port=5432;Database=myrestaurant;Username=myrestaurant;Password=myrestaurant

# --- Data protection keys (§3.4) -----------------------------------------------------------------
# A named volume in compose; back it up alongside the database or TOTP secrets/cookies are lost.
DATA_PROTECTION_KEYS_DIRECTORY=/var/lib/myrestaurant/dataprotection

# --- Timing knobs --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
KITCHEN_SUBMISSION_REMINDER_SECONDS=60   # §10.2, min 1
TABLE_JOIN_TOKEN_ROTATION_SECONDS=60     # §4.3, min 10
TABLE_JOIN_GRANT_MINUTES=10              # §4.4, min 1
TABLE_DISPLAY_PAIRING_CODE_MINUTES=10    # §4.2, min 1

# --- Guest registration rate limit (§11.8, §17) --------------------------------------------------
# /register is anonymous and creates accounts, so it is rate-limited per client address.
#
# READ THE PARTITION BEFORE TIGHTENING THESE. The limit is counted per client address, and over the
# Cloudflare tunnel every guest on the restaurant's own wifi presents the SAME address — so this is a
# per-venue budget, not a per-person one. The default is 60 attempts per 10 minutes because it has to
# cover a full room turning over, with retries, all sharing one bucket. Too loose costs you spam
# accounts, which hold no capability (a guest is the absence of a grant). Too tight costs you a seated
# guest who cannot create the account they need in order to order dinner, at a table where staff have
# no remedy and no diagnosis. Raise these if a busy service ever reports refusals.
GUEST_REGISTRATION_ATTEMPTS_PER_WINDOW=60   # §11.8, min 10
GUEST_REGISTRATION_WINDOW_MINUTES=10        # §11.8, min 1

# --- Argon2id (§3.2 + startup floor guard) -------------------------------------------------------
# The app refuses to start below the floor: memory >= 19456 KiB, iterations >= 2, parallelism >= 1.
ARGON2_MEMORY_KIBIBYTES=65536
ARGON2_ITERATIONS=3
ARGON2_PARALLELISM=1
ARGON2_MAX_CONCURRENT_HASHES=4

# --- Backups (§15) -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A backup set is TWO files sharing one timestamp: the database dump and the Data Protection key ring
# (myrestaurant-<stamp>.dump and myrestaurant-<stamp>-dataprotection.tar). Without the ring, every
# stored TOTP secret is undecryptable — the accounts come back and the enrolled authenticators do not
# (OPERATIONS §6 and §8). scripts/backup.sh writes both, scripts/restore.sh puts both back, and
# scripts/restore_drill.sh rehearses the round trip against a scratch database it creates and
# destroys — it never writes to this one.
BACKUP_DIRECTORY=/var/lib/myrestaurant/backups
BACKUP_SCHEDULE_TIME=03:30
BACKUP_RETENTION_COUNT=14
# The backup and restore scripts find the postgres and web containers by name and REFUSE when more
# than one matches, because dumping the wrong database looks exactly like success. Set these to skip
# discovery — required in CI, and useful whenever a second postgres container is around (the drill
# starts one on purpose).
# POSTGRES_CONTAINER=myrestaurant_postgres_1
# WEB_CONTAINER=myrestaurant_web_1
# Which container engine scripts/backup.sh and scripts/restore_drill.sh use. Unset is right on a host
# with one engine. On a host with BOTH — every GitHub Actions runner is one, since its image installs
# a static podman bundle next to Docker — the two scripts differ in what they can work out for
# themselves: backup.sh asks each engine whether it can see the container it was told to dump and uses
# the one that can, while the drill creates its own container and so has nothing to infer from. Set
# this when the containers you mean belong to a specific engine (F-43).
# CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman
# The scratch image the drill restores into. Fully qualified so a short-name registry prompt cannot
# hang an unattended run.
# DRILL_POSTGRES_IMAGE=docker.io/library/postgres:17-alpine

# --- OpenTelemetry (optional, §12) ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Empty by default; when empty the app attaches no OTLP exporter (no connection-refused noise). Fill
# these in to export — for example OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://otlp.example.com and
# OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=authorization=Bearer <token>.
#
# ASSIGNED EMPTY RATHER THAN COMMENTED OUT (F-57), and that matters more here than anywhere else in
# this file. Every variable compose.yaml interpolates must be assigned, because on an engine that does
# not apply the default after ':-' — Debian trixie's podman-compose does not — a commented-out line
# leaves the placeholder text to reach the container. An EMPTY endpoint switches the exporter off; the
# literal string `${OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT:-}` is not empty, so it switches the exporter ON and
# points it at a hostname made of braces. scripts/check_compose_substitution.sh tells you whether your
# engine needs this file at all.
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=myrestaurant
# run.sh also accepts a legacy UPTRACE_DSN and translates it into the OTEL_* variables above.
# UPTRACE_DSN=

# --- Production tunnel (production profile only, §14.1) ------------------------------------------
# PRODUCTION: set to your Cloudflare named-tunnel token. Required by `--profile production`; empty
# here, and assigned rather than commented out for the reason recorded beside the OTEL_* pair (F-57).
CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN=

# --- Detached test instance (scripts/dev_instance.sh, §14.3a, OPERATIONS §10a) --------------------
# Read from the shell environment by that script, not from this file — nothing here is sourced by a
# script (compose reads this file; the scripts do not). Listed so the knobs are discoverable, with
# the defaults each one overrides.
#
# Do NOT set RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN above for a dev_instance.sh run. That script derives the
# origin from the tunnel hostname and exports it, and the process environment beats this file, so a
# pinned value here is ignored and only succeeds in making this file disagree with what is served.
# What cloudflared points at, and what readiness is probed on. An IPv4 literal, not a name: the web
# port above is published on 127.0.0.1 and nowhere else, and BusyBox wget does not try a second
# address when the first refuses (F-56).
# TUNNEL_TARGET=http://127.0.0.1:8080
# TUNNEL_URL_WAIT=120
# How long postgres is given to accept a connection, and the application to answer /healthz/ready.
# Both waits end EARLY when the thing they are waiting for has stopped, so these are ceilings for a
# slow host rather than the time a broken bring-up takes to report itself (F-55).
# DEV_INSTANCE_DATABASE_WAIT=180
# DEV_INSTANCE_READY_WAIT=300
# How many times a stopped container is started again before `up` gives up on it, and how many engine
# restarts count as a crash loop. Both are the early exits above.
# DEV_INSTANCE_START_ATTEMPTS=3
# DEV_INSTANCE_CRASH_LOOP_RESTARTS=3
# Log lines printed per container when a bring-up fails, and by `dev_instance.sh diagnose`.
# DEV_INSTANCE_LOG_TAIL=40
# How long `up` re-probes the PUBLIC origin before releasing the terminal. The point is that the
# terminal is released on evidence rather than on a return code; 0 disables the check.
# DEV_INSTANCE_SETTLE_SECONDS=20
# DEV_INSTANCE_TUNNEL_CONTAINER=myrestaurant_quicktunnel
# DEV_INSTANCE_STATE_DIRECTORY=${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/myrestaurant
# Fully qualified, for the same reason as DRILL_POSTGRES_IMAGE above and every image in
# compose.yaml (F-51): a short name needs an unqualified-search registry list that Debian does not
# ship populated.
# CLOUDFLARED_IMAGE=docker.io/cloudflare/cloudflared:latest
# Stamped into the image as a build argument and reported by /source (§11.9). dev_instance.sh
# defaults it to `git rev-parse HEAD`, so a tester's bug report names a commit.
# SOURCE_REVISION=

# Dependency updates.

# a bump is only interesting if the suite still passes with it, and until this slice there was
# nothing to ask.

# lands in the one file that pins versions. Dependabot never proposes a prerelease for a dependency
# that is currently on a stable version, which is exactly the project's rule (no prerelease
# packages) without needing to say so.

version: 2

--- METADATA ---
  Relative path:         .github/workflows/ci.yml
  Size:                  24.4 KiB (25022 bytes)
  SHA-256:               419beb3279573eb376fc5556df174e8833090ba88426c85f35f0ecc8654eb747

--- CONTENT ---
# Continuous integration (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §16.4).
#
# Six gates. None of them can be satisfied by a tree that merely looks right:
#
#   tree            The tree is machine-readable at all: no context-dump separators, no
#                   whitespace-only lines, LF endings with a final newline, and every MSBuild and
#                   YAML file parses. Cheapest gate in the workflow and the one that catches the
#                   damage that disguises itself as a toolchain fault — see scripts/check_tree.sh
#                   for the incident that put it here.
#
#   governance      A security policy exists, README/CONTRIBUTING/SECURITY each point at the
#                   others, and no tracked file asserts a GitHub repository setting. That half is
#                   blocking and needs only git and grep. A second, advisory half reads the API and
#                   reports what the published repository actually says — advisory because a fork's
#                   settings are the fork's business. See scripts/check_repository.sh for the
#                   finding that put it here: every gate was green while the repository offered a
#                   reader nowhere to report a defect, and the one document that addressed the
#                   question was wrong about it.
#
#   shell-scripts   Every tracked *.sh parses (`bash -n`) and passes shellcheck. This is the
#                   project's own pre-delivery discipline, enforced instead of remembered.
#
#   build-and-test  Restore, a Release build with warnings escalated to errors, then the whole
#                   xUnit suite. The data-access tests start real PostgreSQL 17 containers through
#                   Testcontainers; a GitHub runner has a Docker socket, so those tests RUN here
#                   rather than skipping the way they do on a machine with no container engine.
#
#   boot-smoke      The production Containerfile is built and the resulting image is booted against
#                   a real PostgreSQL, and /healthz/ready must answer 200. This is the only gate
#                   that proves DbUp migrations apply and the composition root resolves — a class of
#                   failure no unit test sees, because it happens exactly once, at startup, and
#                   presents as a 500 on some route hours later.
#
#                   It then backs that instance up with scripts/backup.sh and puts the result through
#                   scripts/restore_drill.sh (§15), so recovery is rehearsed on every push instead of
#                   being a runbook nobody has executed. It lives here rather than in a job of its
#                   own because everything the drill needs — a built image, a migrated database, a
#                   live Data Protection key ring — is already standing up in this job.
#
#   end-to-end      The §16.3 Playwright scenarios, in Chromium, against the built application. Its
#                   own job rather than part of build-and-test, for two reasons: the scenarios are
#                   opt-in (MYRESTAURANT_E2E) so a workstation `dotnet test` never downloads a
#                   browser by surprise, and a browser-driven flake should be attributable at a
#                   glance instead of hiding inside a nine-hundred-fact summary.
#
# The workflow is also callable (`workflow_call`) so the release pipeline runs precisely these
# gates before it publishes an image, rather than a copy of them that can drift.

name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_call:
    # Declared, and optional. A called workflow sees only the secrets it is handed, so without
    # this the governance job's advisory half would silently skip on the one run that publishes
    # an image — the run whose settings report is worth the most (F-46). Optional because a fork
    # will not have the secret and the half it feeds is advisory anyway.
    secrets:
      ADMIN_READ_TOKEN:
        required: false
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

# A second push to the same ref makes the first answer irrelevant, so cancel it. Keyed on the ref
# rather than the workflow so a tag build and a branch build never cancel each other.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  DOTNET_NOLOGO: "true"
  DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: "true"
  DOTNET_SKIP_FIRST_TIME_EXPERIENCE: "true"
  NUGET_XMLDOC_MODE: skip

jobs:
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Tree hygiene. Seconds, no SDK, no containers, no network beyond the checkout.
  #
  # A job of its own rather than a step bolted onto shell-scripts, for two reasons. It is not about
  # shell: the file it exists to protect is XML, and the incident that produced it took out the
  # build for every project in the solution. And a distinct check name means a failure here is
  # attributable from the commit list without opening anything — which is the whole point of a gate
  # whose failure mode is a message that blames the wrong tool.
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  tree:
    name: tree hygiene
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: check out
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Blocking, all five of its gates. PyYAML is preinstalled on GitHub's Ubuntu runners, so the
      # YAML parse — the one gate that degrades to a skip on a workstation without it — runs here.
      - name: the tree parses
        run: bash scripts/check_tree.sh

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Repository governance. The layer every other gate in this file is blind to.
  #
  # Its own job for the same reason `tree` has one: a distinct check name makes a failure
  # attributable from the commit list. But the deeper reason it is separate is that half of it is
  # advisory, and a job that mixes a blocking assertion with an advisory report teaches nobody
  # which one just spoke.
  #
  # administration:read is requested for exactly one call — the private-vulnerability-reporting
  # endpoint — and is scoped to this job rather than the workflow. On a fork's pull request the
  # token will not carry it; the script reports that as unknown rather than as a finding, which is
  # why this job stays green there.
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  governance:
    name: repository governance
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: check out
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # The tree half blocks. The platform half warns and never moves the exit code, so a
      # repository setting nobody has clicked yet cannot hold up a build — it just says so, on
      # every run, until somebody clicks it.
      - name: the governance surface, and the published settings
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ADMIN_READ_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/check_repository.sh

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Shell scripts. Also cheap, so it runs alongside everything else and fails in ~30 seconds.
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  shell-scripts:
    name: shell scripts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: check out
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: parse every tracked script
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mapfile -t scripts < <(git ls-files '*.sh')
          printf 'checking %d script(s)\n' "${#scripts[@]}"
          for script in "${scripts[@]}"; do
              printf '  bash -n %s\n' "$script"
              bash -n "$script"
          done

      - name: install shellcheck
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends shellcheck
          shellcheck --version

      # Blocking at `warning`. Every script in the tree is clean at `style` today, but the gate sits
      # one notch lower on purpose: a shellcheck upgrade that adds a new style check would otherwise
      # turn a build red on a day nobody touched the repository, and that is how people learn to
      # ignore a red build. The stricter pass runs below, advisory only.
      - name: shellcheck (blocking, severity=warning)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mapfile -t scripts < <(git ls-files '*.sh')
          shellcheck --severity=warning --color=always "${scripts[@]}"

      - name: shellcheck (advisory, severity=style)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mapfile -t scripts < <(git ls-files '*.sh')
          shellcheck --severity=style --color=always "${scripts[@]}"

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4. Build and the full test suite, with warnings as errors.
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  build-and-test:
    name: build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    steps:
      - name: check out
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # 10.0.x rather than global.json's exact pin: global.json says 10.0.100 with
      # rollForward=latestMinor, so any 10.0 SDK satisfies it, and asking for an exact patch that
      # has since been delisted is a needless way to fail.
      - name: set up the .NET SDK
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
        with:
          dotnet-version: "10.0.x"

      # There are no packages.lock.json files, so setup-dotnet's own cache input cannot be used;
      # key the global-packages folder on the only files that can change a restore graph.
      - name: cache NuGet packages
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.nuget/packages
          key: nuget-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('Directory.Packages.props', 'global.json', '**/*.csproj') }}
          restore-keys: |
            nuget-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: dotnet --info
        run: dotnet --info

      - name: restore
        run: dotnet restore MyRestaurant.slnx

      # ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true flips TreatWarningsAsErrors in Directory.Build.props (and
      # makes the build deterministic). A plain `dotnet build` on a developer's clone stays lenient.
      - name: build (Release, warnings as errors)
        run: |
          dotnet build MyRestaurant.slnx \
              --configuration Release \
              --no-restore \
              -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true

      # Testcontainers finds /var/run/docker.sock on the runner, so the ~190 data-access integration
      # facts execute here. MYRESTAURANT_E2E is deliberately NOT set: the §16.3 scenarios have their
      # own job below, and running them twice would double the browser time for one answer.
      #
      # MICROSOFT.TESTING.PLATFORM MODE, not VSTest (F-97). `global.json` carries the opt-in, so the
      # command line is the MTP one: the solution arrives through `--solution` rather than as a bare
      # argument, `--logger` does not exist here, and the TRX report is xUnit.net's own reporter asked
      # for after the `--` that marks where test-application arguments begin. `--output Detailed` is
      # what `console;verbosity=normal` used to buy.
      - name: test
        run: |
          dotnet test --solution MyRestaurant.slnx \
              --configuration Release \
              --no-build \
              -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true \
              --output Detailed \
              --results-directory "${{ github.workspace }}/TestResults" \
              -- --report-xunit-trx

      - name: upload test results
        if: ${{ always() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: test-results
          path: "**/TestResults/**/*.trx"
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

      # Advisory. A published advisory against a package we already depend on is real news, but it
      # arrives without a commit, so it reports rather than blocks (see Directory.Build.props).
      - name: vulnerable package audit (advisory)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: dotnet list MyRestaurant.slnx package --vulnerable --include-transitive

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. Boot the actual production image against an actual PostgreSQL, then rehearse recovery from it.
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  boot-smoke:
    name: boot smoke (container image)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30

    # compose.yaml is deliberately not used here: its data-protection volume carries Podman's ':U'
    # suffix (ADR-0004 — rootless Podman is canonical), which Docker Compose rejects outright. A
    # service container plus one `docker run` is the same topology with none of that argument.
    # Fully qualified, like every other image reference in this repository (§14.1, F-60). Docker
    # normalises `postgres:17-alpine` to exactly this reference, so on this runner the two forms name
    # the same image and the same layer cache — which means writing it out costs nothing here and
    # makes one rule true of the whole tree instead of true of compose.yaml and the restore drill.
    services:
      postgres:
        image: docker.io/library/postgres:17-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: myrestaurant
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: myrestaurant
          POSTGRES_DB: myrestaurant
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U myrestaurant -d myrestaurant"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 20

    steps:
      - name: check out
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # SOURCE_REVISION is what turns "some build of main" into an identifiable one: it becomes the
      # assembly's informational version, which becomes /source's answer and OpenTelemetry's
      # service.version (§11.9, §12). Passing it here is also what lets the step below assert the
      # whole chain actually works.
      - name: build the runtime image
        run: |
          docker build --file Containerfile --tag myrestaurant_web:ci \
              --build-arg SOURCE_REVISION="${{ github.sha }}" \
              .

      # --network host so the container reaches the service database on the runner's published
      # 127.0.0.1:5432 and publishes its own 8080 back to the runner for the probe below.
      - name: start it against the service database
        run: |
          docker run --detach --name myrestaurant_web_ci --network host \
              --env RESTAURANT_NAME="CI Restaurant" \
              --env RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN="https://localhost:8443" \
              --env RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE="America/New_York" \
              --env RESTAURANT_CLOCK_FORMAT="12-hour" \
              --env RESTAURANT_CURRENCY_CODE="USD" \
              --env RESTAURANT_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING="Host=127.0.0.1;Port=5432;Database=myrestaurant;Username=myrestaurant;Password=myrestaurant" \
              --env DATA_PROTECTION_KEYS_DIRECTORY="/var/lib/myrestaurant/dataprotection" \
              myrestaurant_web:ci

      - name: wait for /healthz/ready
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          deadline=$(( SECONDS + 180 ))
          while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
              if ! docker inspect --format '{{.State.Running}}' myrestaurant_web_ci | grep --quiet true; then
                  echo "the web container exited before it became ready" >&2
                  exit 1
              fi
              if curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz/ready; then
                  echo
                  echo "ready: config bound, migrations applied, database reachable."
                  curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 5 http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz/live
                  echo
                  exit 0
              fi
              sleep 3
          done
          echo "/healthz/ready did not answer 200 within 180s" >&2
          exit 1

      # Data Protection creates its first key the first time it protects anything, and
      # /healthz/ready protects nothing — so on a freshly booted instance the key ring is an empty
      # directory. /setup renders a form, which mints an antiforgery token, which mints the key.
      # Without this step the drill's key-ring gate would report an empty ring on every run and
      # would therefore stop meaning anything.
      - name: render a page so a Data Protection key exists
        run: |
          curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 10 --output /dev/null \
              http://127.0.0.1:8080/setup
          echo "/setup rendered; the key ring is no longer empty."

      # The source offer must name the revision it is offering the source OF (§11.9, AGPL §13), and
      # that answer travels a long way to get onto the page: a build argument, an MSBuild property, an
      # assembly attribute, a parse, a component. Every link in that chain is silent when it breaks —
      # the page still renders, and it renders "not recorded", which looks like a configuration choice
      # rather than a defect. So the gate is the commit itself appearing in the response, which is
      # exactly the assertion nothing weaker can be satisfied by.
      #
      # It doubles as an anonymous-reachability check: no cookie is sent, so a regression that put the
      # licence offer behind authentication would fail here.
      - name: the source offer names this commit
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          page=$(curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 10 http://127.0.0.1:8080/source)
          if ! grep --quiet --fixed-strings "${{ github.sha }}" <<<"$page"; then
              echo "/source did not report this build's revision (${{ github.sha }})." >&2
              echo "--- what it said instead ---" >&2
              printf '%s\n' "$page" >&2
              exit 1
          fi
          echo "/source reports ${{ github.sha }} and answered anonymously."

      # POSTGRES_CONTAINER and WEB_CONTAINER are set rather than discovered: the service container's
      # name is generated by the runner, and scripts/backup.sh refuses to guess when more than one
      # container matches its filter — which is exactly the situation the drill's own scratch
      # container creates a few seconds later.
      #
      # CONTAINER_ENGINE=docker is the load-bearing line here (F-43). This runner image installs a
      # static podman bundle alongside Docker, so `command -v podman` succeeds on it — and every
      # container in this job, the service database included, belongs to the Docker daemon. Without
      # this, scripts/backup.sh reached for podman, `podman exec <a docker container id>` failed with
      # "no such container", and the script reported it as the database not answering pg_isready:
      # a message that sends a reader to PostgreSQL for a fault that is entirely in engine selection.
      # The script now also infers the engine from the container it was given, so this is belt and
      # braces — but it is the half that is obvious from the job, which is where it belongs.
      #
      # The backup set is deliberately NOT uploaded as an artifact. The -dataprotection.tar is key
      # material in the clear; it is throwaway here, but publishing one is not a habit worth forming.
      - name: back up the booted instance
        env:
          BACKUP_DIRECTORY: ${{ github.workspace }}/ci-backups
          CONTAINER_ENGINE: docker
          POSTGRES_CONTAINER: ${{ job.services.postgres.id }}
          WEB_CONTAINER: myrestaurant_web_ci
        run: bash scripts/backup.sh

      # Not --strict on this first landing. Every FAIL gate still blocks; what --strict adds is that
      # ignored pg_restore errors and an empty key ring also fail, and neither number has been
      # observed on a real run yet. Once a few runs report "pg_restore completed with no errors",
      # tightening this is a one-word edit.
      #
      # CONTAINER_ENGINE=docker for a second reason as well as the first. The drill creates its own
      # scratch container, so either engine would work — but this exact image is already in the Docker
      # daemon's store, because the service container above pulled it. Left to its default the drill
      # would pull the same image again into podman's store, and pay for it on every push.
      #
      # The reference is spelled the same way as the service container's, which is what keeps that
      # sentence true: Docker normalises a short name to `docker.io/library/…`, so the qualified form
      # is a hit in the store rather than a second pull. Writing both out fully is §14.1's rule
      # applied to every image reference in the tree rather than to two of them (F-60).
      - name: drill the restore
        env:
          BACKUP_DIRECTORY: ${{ github.workspace }}/ci-backups
          CONTAINER_ENGINE: docker
          DRILL_POSTGRES_IMAGE: docker.io/library/postgres:17-alpine
        run: bash scripts/restore_drill.sh

      - name: container logs
        if: ${{ failure() }}
        run: docker logs myrestaurant_web_ci

      - name: stop the container
        if: ${{ always() }}
        run: docker rm --force myrestaurant_web_ci || true

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 6. The §16.3 end-to-end scenarios, in a real browser.
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  end-to-end:
    name: end to end (Playwright)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - name: check out
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: set up the .NET SDK
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
        with:
          dotnet-version: "10.0.x"

      - name: cache NuGet packages
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.nuget/packages
          key: nuget-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('Directory.Packages.props', 'global.json', '**/*.csproj') }}
          restore-keys: |
            nuget-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: restore
        run: dotnet restore MyRestaurant.slnx

      # The harness boots the web application from its own build output, so this build is not merely
      # a prerequisite for the test assembly — it produces the binary under test.
      - name: build (Release, warnings as errors)
        run: |
          dotnet build MyRestaurant.slnx \
              --configuration Release \
              --no-restore \
              -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true

      # The harness calls `playwright install chromium` itself, which downloads the browser but not
      # its system libraries. --with-deps needs apt and therefore root, which a test process has no
      # business asking for — so it happens here, once, through the wrapper the build produced.
      # pwsh is preinstalled on GitHub's Ubuntu runners.
      - name: cache Playwright browsers
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
          key: playwright-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('Directory.Packages.props') }}
          restore-keys: |
            playwright-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: install Chromium and its dependencies
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          pwsh tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/bin/Release/net10.0/playwright.ps1 \
              install --with-deps chromium

      # MYRESTAURANT_E2E is what turns the sixteen placeholders into real scenarios. Testcontainers
      # reaches the runner's Docker socket for the shared PostgreSQL 17 container; each scenario then
      # creates its own database on it and boots the application on its own loopback port.
      - name: run the §16.3 scenarios
        env:
          MYRESTAURANT_E2E: "1"
        run: |
          dotnet test --project tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests.csproj \
              --configuration Release \
              --no-build \
              -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true \
              --output Detailed \
              --results-directory "${{ github.workspace }}/TestResults" \
              -- --report-xunit-trx

        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7

--- METADATA ---
  Relative path:         .github/workflows/release.yml
  Size:                  8.6 KiB (8780 bytes)
  SHA-256:               fc6d24f98ec594bb8cc99c121cbc8a830f92e84e75037d1739d3774ca5c98912

--- CONTENT ---
# Publish the container image on a tag (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §16.4: "publish image on tag").
#
# The gates are not re-declared here. `verify` calls .github/workflows/ci.yml, so a release runs the
# same shell lint, the same strict build, the same test suite and the same boot smoke that every
# push runs — a second copy of them would be a second copy to keep correct.
#
# Tagging:
#     git tag --annotate v1.0.0 --message 'M6 complete'
#     git push origin v1.0.0
#
# Result: ghcr.io/<owner>/<repository>:1.0.0, :1.0, and :sha-<commit>. See docs/OPERATIONS.md §14
# for how to deploy from the registry instead of building on the box. The example matches the
# procedure in that section on purpose: this comment and OPERATIONS §14 named two different
# versions for one release for as long as both existed, which is a small thing to get wrong and an
# irritating one to meet halfway through a tag.
#
# The tag is also what the image says about itself: `verify` proves the tree, then the version is
# derived from the tag and the commit and passed into the build, so a running instance answers
# /source with the same numbers the registry used (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §11.9). Finally a GitHub
# release is opened on the tag, because a published image with no release note is a thing people have
# to reverse-engineer from a manifest.

name: release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

# Never cancel a release in flight: a half-pushed manifest is worse than a slow one.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: verify
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Named rather than `secrets: inherit`. The governance job's advisory half reads the GitHub
    # API and reports the published settings, and a release is the run where that report is worth
    # the most — it is the run that creates the package whose visibility nothing in this tree can
    # see (F-46). One secret, passed on purpose, is a smaller statement than all of them.
    secrets:
      ADMIN_READ_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ADMIN_READ_TOKEN }}

  image:
    name: publish image
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.value }}

    steps:
      - name: check out the tag
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: set up buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4

      - name: sign in to ghcr.io
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Derived in a step rather than taken from metadata-action's outputs, because the image needs
      # the bare version string as a build argument and reading it back out of a tag list is one more
      # thing that can silently produce the wrong answer. Both values arrive through `env:` rather
      # than being interpolated into the script body: a ref name is attacker-influencable on a fork,
      # and `${{ }}` inside `run:` is textual substitution before the shell ever sees it.
      - name: derive the version from the tag
        id: version
        env:
          REFERENCE_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          REFERENCE_TYPE: ${{ github.ref_type }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$REFERENCE_TYPE" = 'tag' ]; then
              version="${REFERENCE_NAME#v}"
          else
              # workflow_dispatch off a branch. Publishing 1.0.0 from an untagged branch would be a
              # lie the registry then caches, so say what it actually is.
              version="0.0.0-${REFERENCE_NAME//[^0-9A-Za-z.-]/-}"
          fi
          printf 'value=%s\n' "$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          printf 'the image will report version %s at revision %s\n' "$version" "${{ github.sha }}"

      - name: derive tags and labels
        id: metadata
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v6
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
          tags: |
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}
            type=sha,format=long
          labels: |
            org.opencontainers.image.title=MyRestaurant
            org.opencontainers.image.description=Self-hosted, single-restaurant ordering system
            org.opencontainers.image.licenses=AGPL-3.0-only

      # linux/amd64 only, deliberately. The Containerfile runs a full `dotnet publish` inside the
      # build stage, and doing that for arm64 under QEMU emulation takes long enough to time out.
      # An arm64 image wants a cross-compiled publish (-r linux-arm64 from an amd64 SDK) rather than
      # an emulated one; that is a Containerfile change, not a workflow line, so it is not here.
      - name: build and push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: .
          file: ./Containerfile
          platforms: linux/amd64
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.labels }}
          # What the running instance will say about itself (§11.9). Without these the published
          # image reports Directory.Build.props' VersionPrefix and no revision at all — which is to
          # say, every release would claim to be the same build.
          build-args: |
            VERSION=${{ steps.version.outputs.value }}
            SOURCE_REVISION=${{ github.sha }}

      - name: summarize
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          {
              echo "### Published"
              echo
              echo '```'
              printf '%s\n' "${{ steps.metadata.outputs.tags }}"
              echo '```'
              echo
              echo "Version: \`${{ steps.version.outputs.value }}\` at \`${{ github.sha }}\`."
              echo "A running instance reports the same at \`/source\`."
              echo
              echo "Pull with: \`podman pull ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:\${TAG}\`"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The release note. Separate from `image` and downstream of it, so a failed push cannot leave a
  # release advertising an image that is not in the registry.
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  release-notes:
    name: publish release notes
    needs: image
    if: ${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      # The only job in either workflow that writes anything to the repository. Scoped here rather
      # than raised at the workflow level for that reason.
      contents: write

    steps:
      - name: check out the tag
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # Idempotent on purpose: re-running a release (or dispatching one twice) should update the note
      # rather than fail on "already exists". --verify-tag refuses to invent a tag that is not there,
      # which is the one mistake worth being loud about.
      - name: open or update the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.image.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          notes="$(mktemp)"
          {
              echo "### Container image"
              echo
              echo '```bash'
              echo "podman pull ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${VERSION}"
              echo '```'
              echo
              echo "Built from \`${{ github.sha }}\`, \`linux/amd64\`."
              echo
              echo "### Verifying what you are running"
              echo
              echo "Every page links to \`/source\` in its footer. That page reports this version and"
              echo "revision, and offers the corresponding source under AGPL-3.0-only."
              echo
              echo "### Reading further"
              echo
              echo "- Deploying from the registry: \`docs/OPERATIONS.md\` §14"
              echo "- What changed and why: \`docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md\`"
              echo "- Configuration: \`.env.example\` and \`docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md\` §13"
          } > "$notes"

          if gh release view "$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              gh release edit "$TAG" --notes-file "$notes"
              echo "updated the existing release for $TAG"
          else
              gh release create "$TAG" --title "$TAG" --notes-file "$notes" --verify-tag
              echo "created the release for $TAG"
          fi

# Contributing

Thank you for your interest — but this repository does not accept outside contributions.

This is a single-owner project, published so that anyone may **read, run, fork, and modify their own copy** under the AGPL-3.0-only license. It is not developed in the open in the collaborative sense:

- **There is no bug tracker.** Nothing filed here is triaged, and nothing filed here is a queue anybody works. If the issue tab is open on the day you read this, that is a fallback for the one case described in `SECURITY.md`, not an invitation.
- **Pull requests are closed unreviewed.** GitHub does not allow refusing them outright on a public repository, so this file is the notice: unsolicited pull requests will be closed without review, whatever their merit. Nothing personal.
- **All copyright remains with the authors.** No contributor license agreement exists because no contributions are accepted.

If you want a change, fork it — the AGPL guarantees you that freedom, and your fork owes its users the same.

## The one exception: security

**A vulnerability report is not a contribution, and `SECURITY.md` is the door for it.**

The distinction is not a courtesy. Refusing a feature costs the person who wanted the feature, and they have the source and the freedom to build it themselves — that is the arrangement, and it is a fair one. Refusing a report about a forgeable capability token costs somebody's *guests*, who never chose this software, cannot read this file, and have no fork to run. So the two things get opposite answers.

Read `SECURITY.md` before reporting: it names the private channel, and it points at the accepted-risks register (`docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md` §17) so that a decision already argued and written down does not cost you an evening. **Do not send the fix as a pull request** — that publishes the defect in a diff before there is a release to upgrade to.

## A note on what this file may claim

This document used to say that the issue tracker had been switched off. It had not been, and had never been — the setting was on for as long as the sentence existed, so the only document addressing the question was wrong about it, and the sentence stood because nothing in a repository can inspect its own settings page. That is finding **F-42**.

The rule that came out of it, enforced by `scripts/check_repository.sh` rather than remembered: **a document in this tree states policy, never platform state.** "Nothing filed here is triaged" is true wherever it is read and survives somebody toggling a checkbox. A claim about the checkbox is true only until the checkbox moves, and no gate can tell you when that happened.

## For the owner (and the owner's tooling)

Changes to this repository follow the **atomic documentation** rule (`REQUIREMENTS.md` §10, technical specification §18): a behavior change lands in **one commit** together with its `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md` edit, its `docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md` edit, a `docs/DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md` ledger row where a finding is involved, and edits to any affected `docs/adr/` record. ADRs are edited **in place** with a dated History line — never duplicated, never superseded by a new file. No implementation is complete until the code and every document describing it agree.

# Dev-profile reverse proxy (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §14.1). Caddy terminates TLS at
# https://localhost:8443 using its internal CA and forwards to the web container over HTTP.

# Blazor Server WebSocket, so no extra configuration is needed for live updates.

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# Multi-stage build for the web application (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §14.1, BUILD_PROGRESS).
#   * build stage: the .NET SDK restores and publishes a Release build;
#   * runtime stage: the smaller ASP.NET runtime image, plus tzdata (the app resolves
#     RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE through TimeZoneInfo — globalization is NOT invariant) and curl
#     (the compose healthchecks call /healthz/* with it).
#
# Build context is the repository root so Central Package Management files resolve during restore —
# but `.dockerignore` reduces that root to an allow-list first, and the guard below asserts that it
# did. See F-45: for the life of this file, `COPY . .` meant the entire working tree, including
# `.git`, `docs/llm/`, every test project, and — on a host that had ever taken a backup or run the
# application — `.env`, the Data Protection key ring, and the `-dataprotection.tar` that
# OPERATIONS §8 calls the key material in the clear.

# ---- build -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build
WORKDIR /source

# What this build is (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §11.9). VERSION defaults to Directory.Build.props'
# VersionPrefix so a plain `podman build` with no arguments still produces something coherent;
# SOURCE_REVISION is empty unless a pipeline supplies it, and an empty one is reported as "not
# recorded" rather than guessed at. Both are ARGs rather than a file in the tree because the tree
# does not know its own commit — git metadata is not in the build context, and the .NET SDK only
# appends SourceRevisionId by itself when SourceLink is installed to set
# SourceControlInformationFeatureSupported, which is a package dependency for one string.
ARG VERSION=1.0.0
ARG SOURCE_REVISION=

# Copy the allow-listed context. (Layer caching could be tightened by copying the *.csproj and
# Directory.*.props first and restoring before the rest — deferred; correctness first.)
COPY . .

# The context is what `.dockerignore` says it is — asserted, not assumed.
#
# An ignore-file is an instruction to a tool, and instructions can be renamed, superseded by a
# `.containerignore` that Podman prefers, or overridden with `--ignorefile`. None of those failures
# announce themselves: the build still succeeds, and the only visible symptom is that it took
# longer. So the allow-list is stated twice on purpose — once as the instruction and once here as
# the assertion — and the build stops if the two disagree.
#
# This is a stronger check than a list of forbidden names, and deliberately so. A deny-list has to
# be extended for tomorrow's untracked secret by somebody who remembers to; this fails on any
# top-level entry nobody has thought about yet, which is the population that F-45 was actually
# about. Scope decided in one place, the way scripts/check_tree.sh decides `is_authored_text` —
# see F-41.
RUN set -eu; \
    unexpected=''; \
    for entry in * .[!.]*; do \
        [ -e "$entry" ] || continue; \
        case "$entry" in \
            .editorconfig|Directory.Build.props|Directory.Packages.props|global.json|src) ;; \
            *) unexpected="${unexpected} ${entry}" ;; \
        esac; \
    done; \
    missing=''; \
    for required in \
        .editorconfig \
        Directory.Build.props \
        Directory.Packages.props \
        global.json \
        src/MyRestaurant.Domain/MyRestaurant.Domain.csproj \
        src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/MyRestaurant.DataAccess.csproj \
        src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.csproj \
    ; do \
        [ -e "$required" ] || missing="${missing} ${required}"; \
    done; \
    stale="$(find src -type d -name bin -o -type d -name obj 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"; \
    if [ -n "$unexpected" ] || [ -n "$missing" ] || [ -n "$stale" ]; then \
        echo 'BUILD CONTEXT REJECTED — .dockerignore did not take effect (see F-45).' >&2; \
        [ -z "$unexpected" ] || echo "  not allowed here:  ${unexpected# }" >&2; \
        [ -z "$missing" ]    || echo "  required, absent:  ${missing# }" >&2; \
        [ -z "$stale" ]      || echo "  local build output:${stale%% }" >&2; \
        echo '' >&2; \
        echo '  The context root must contain exactly: .editorconfig Directory.Build.props' >&2; \
        echo '  Directory.Packages.props global.json src' >&2; \
        echo '' >&2; \
        echo '  Most likely: .dockerignore is missing from the context root, a .containerignore' >&2; \
        echo '  is shadowing it (podman prefers that name when both exist), or --ignorefile was' >&2; \
        echo '  passed. Anything else here was copied into this builder, and on a host that has' >&2; \
        echo '  taken a backup that includes the Data Protection key ring in the clear.' >&2; \
        exit 1; \
    fi; \
    echo "build context accepted: $(find . -type f | wc -l) file(s)"

# ${SOURCE_REVISION:+...} expands to "+<revision>" only when the argument is set and non-empty, so an
# unstamped build gets a clean "1.0.0" rather than a trailing "+" that BuildInformation would have to
# treat as a revision it does not have.
RUN INFORMATIONAL_VERSION="${VERSION}${SOURCE_REVISION:++${SOURCE_REVISION}}" \
    && echo "building MyRestaurant ${INFORMATIONAL_VERSION}" \
    && dotnet publish src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.csproj \
        --configuration Release \
        --output /app/publish \
        /p:UseAppHost=false \
        /p:Version="${VERSION}" \
        /p:InformationalVersion="${INFORMATIONAL_VERSION}"

# ---- runtime -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 AS runtime
WORKDIR /app

# tzdata for TimeZoneInfo; curl for the container healthcheck. Clean apt lists to keep the layer small.
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends tzdata curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY --from=build /app/publish .

# The app is only reached through the trusted proxy, so it serves plain HTTP inside the network.
ENV ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://+:8080 \
    ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production \
    DOTNET_EnableDiagnostics=0

EXPOSE 8080

ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "MyRestaurant.WebApplication.dll"]

<Project>

  <!--
    Solution-wide build settings. Package *versions* live in Directory.Packages.props
    (central package management); nothing else in the tree pins a version (REQUIREMENTS §2,
    TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §16). Keep this file free of per-package references.
  -->
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <LangVersion>latest</LangVersion>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <InvariantGlobalization>false</InvariantGlobalization>
    <!--
      The application resolves RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE through TimeZoneInfo, so globalization
      must stay on and the runtime container installs tzdata (BUILD_PROGRESS: known caveats).
      Do not set InvariantGlobalization=true.
    -->
  </PropertyGroup>

  <PropertyGroup>
    <EnableNETAnalyzers>true</EnableNETAnalyzers>
    <AnalysisLevel>latest</AnalysisLevel>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
    <!--
      Warnings are not errors for a plain `dotnet build`: a fresh clone on a newer SDK must build
      through analyzer drift rather than refusing at the door (README: known caveats).
    -->
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>false</GenerateDocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!--
    ...and they ARE errors in CI, which passes -p:ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true
    (.github/workflows/ci.yml, TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §16.4). This is the answer to the note this
    file carried from M1 — "flip to true once the first green build is established". The first green
    build is long established; what stayed unresolved is that flipping it globally would make a
    fresh clone on tomorrow's SDK fail at the door, which is a worse outcome than a warning nobody
    read. Conditioning on the property CI already sets gets the strictness where it belongs and
    leaves `dotnet build` on a workstation lenient.

    NuGet audit findings (NU1901-NU1904) stay warnings even there. They appear when an advisory is
    published against a package this tree already depends on — real news, but news that arrives on a
    day nobody touched the repository, and a pipeline that turns red without a commit is a pipeline
    people learn to ignore. CI reports them in a dedicated non-blocking step instead.
  -->
  <PropertyGroup Condition="'$(ContinuousIntegrationBuild)' == 'true'">
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <WarningsNotAsErrors>NU1901;NU1902;NU1903;NU1904</WarningsNotAsErrors>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <PropertyGroup>
    <ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>
    <CentralPackageTransitivePinningEnabled>true</CentralPackageTransitivePinningEnabled>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!--
    Identity of the built assemblies (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §11.9, §12).

    VersionPrefix is what an untagged build reports. `Version` defaults to it, `InformationalVersion`
    defaults to `Version`, and the SDK writes the latter into AssemblyInformationalVersionAttribute —
    which is where WebApplication/Configuration/BuildInformation reads it back out. The release
    pipeline overrides Version from the git tag, so the two can disagree only on main between tags,
    which is correct: a build off main is not the release, and saying so is the point.

    The SDK will also append "+$(SourceRevisionId)" by itself, but only when
    SourceControlInformationFeatureSupported is true — a property SourceLink sets and nothing else in
    the SDK does. Rather than take a package dependency to obtain one string, the Containerfile passes
    InformationalVersion explicitly from its VERSION and SOURCE_REVISION build arguments, and the
    workflows fill those in from the tag and the commit. A build that was told neither reports its
    version with no revision, and the /source page says as much rather than inventing one.

    Bumping VersionPrefix is a step in the release procedure (OPERATIONS §14), not something CI does.
  -->
  <PropertyGroup>
    <VersionPrefix>1.0.0</VersionPrefix>
    <Product>MyRestaurant</Product>
    <Company>MyRestaurant</Company>
    <Authors>MyRestaurant</Authors>
    <Description>Self-hosted, single-restaurant ordering system.</Description>
    <Copyright>Copyright (C) 2026 the MyRestaurant authors</Copyright>
  </PropertyGroup>

</Project>

<Project>

  <!--
    Central Package Management. This is the ONE place versions are declared
    (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §16; REQUIREMENTS §2). csproj files use versionless
    <PackageReference> entries.

    Every version below is a STABLE (non-prerelease, non-nightly) release, verified with
    `dotnet list package` in its outdated mode against nuget.org. There is no longer a date
    on that claim: it used to say every pin had been resolved on one day, and three of the
    annotations further down already contradicted it (F-126). Confirm with `dotnet restore`
    on a networked machine; if a version has moved on, bump it here only
    (BUILD_PROGRESS: first-build checklist) and read the API surface of what you bumped AT
    the version you pinned rather than from memory.

    Note that outdated mode only inspects packages a project actually references, so it is
    silent about NSubstitute below — that entry is a version *pin standing ready* for
    §16.1's "NSubstitute acceptable", not a dependency anything currently takes. It is
    checked by hand when this block is refreshed (6.0.0 was current on 2026-08-02).
